title: The Periphery
summary: The edge of spirit sight on the material side.

claims.text: The Periphery is sensing the Otherworlds while still on the mundane side of the Gauntlet, felt as flashes of certainty, a sense of danger or a hint of what is coming.
It touches Sleepers too, chiefly people with a knack for Awareness, though for most of them it amounts to brief glimpses and visits to dream realms.
Mages and Garou agree the Otherworlds have some structure, yet no map holds, since the places shift with each traveler's perception.

title: Etherspace, the Deep Umbra and the Void
summary: Three names for the depths past the Horizon.

claims.text: The Sons of Ether call the deep reaches Etherspace, the other Traditions say Deep Umbra, and the Technocracy speaks of the Void.
No mage claims to understand it; talk of warped spirits, Nephandi Labyrinths and stranger masters still falls short of what is out there.

title: Shade and Shard Realms
summary: The planets as mages travel them.

claims.text: Old tales hold that the One split into the Many: its large pieces became the Shard Realms, meaning the Sun, the nine planets and the Moon, while small bits became spirits and living things.
Each Shard throws a shadow on the Horizon, a Shade Realm, which seems to mirror its planet but departs from the scientific picture in many ways.
A portal is a lasting gateway to a Realm, and a temporary one is called a Gate.

title: The Shadowlands seen by mages
summary: How mages understand the land of the dead.

claims.text: Mages describe the Shadowlands as the memory of what is and what was: anything people cared about intensely echoes there, worn by rot as the feeling fades.
A building hated by thousands of pupils may stand there long after the real one is dust, and the Restless Dead live among these relics as creatures of passion.

title: The race into space
summary: Rival efforts to claim new worlds.

claims.text: Some Sons of Ether race the Technocracy to find Realms and settle planets first, and many of these pioneers fall prey to Nephandi and Marauders in the Void.
Etherjammers and Void Engineers push their craft ever farther into deep space in what mages call the Great Race.

title: The fall of the College on Mus
summary: A Hermetic school lost in the Umbra.

claims.text: After the Second World War the Order of Hermes taught the remnants of the Batini at a College on the Shade Realm of Mus and took in many refugees.
In August 1995 a Technocratic fleet attacked the Chantry; a third force of Umbrood, wormlike beasts and Nephandi then struck both sides and took the College.
Chancellor Gilmore and a few others fled to Horizon by a last portal, while the three remaining Batini teachers stayed behind to destroy the building.

title: The Martian Penumbra
summary: Mars as mages knew it in the mid-1990s.

claims.text: Mars and Venus are the only Realms past the Horizon with Penumbrae of their own; in the Martian one, the canals Schiaparelli described are real.

Two Tradition settlements stand where seven canals meet, the Trivium Charontis: the terraformed grounds of Doissetep, whose great house sits in an overlap zone with the Shade Realm of Forces, and a Sons of Ether camp nicknamed Bradbury, set up with the Deacons' leave in summer 1996.
The settlements live by the slightly longer Martian day but keep records in Greenwich Mean Time.
